skill.name: yescan-ocr-universal
skill.description: Extract, recognize, and structure text from a single image using Yescan OCR. It supports URLs, local image paths, and base64 inputs across 19 OCR scenes.
skill.summary: Run Yescan OCR on one image and return structured text results.
skill.author: yescan-ai

security_audit.summary: Most critical scanner alerts for Windows Credential Manager, certificate keys, entropy, encoded bytes, and markdown backticks are false positives. Confirmed risks are the intended third-party OCR network transfer, API-key handling through environment or ~/.yescan_env, temp-file output for translated images, and two semantic issues involving redirects and shell command construction. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: OCR POST requests allow redirects while carrying the API key and image payload.
remediation.suggestion: Set allow_redirects=False or explicitly validate the final redirect host before any payload is resent.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions rely on shell commands with user-controlled URL, path, or base64 values.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to pass arguments as an argv array or use strict shell escaping for every substituted value.

remediation.issue: The fallback key file stores SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY as plaintext in ~/.yescan_env.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or an OS secret store, and keep the file fallback opt-in with strict permission checks.

remediation.issue: Translated image outputs are written under the temp directory and are not cleaned automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Add retention guidance or a cleanup option for /tmp/imgs outputs that may contain sensitive translated content.

content.user_title: Extract Text from Images with Yescan OCR
content.value_statement: Images often contain text that is hard to reuse. This skill sends one image to Yescan OCR and returns structured recognition results.
actual_capabilities: Accepts one image as a URL, local file path, or base64 string.
Routes requests to 19 OCR scenes, including tables, invoices, IDs, formulas, and product images.
Returns the OCR service response with structured text fields for the selected scene.
Uses a Python CLI wrapper that validates scene names, file size, and image extensions.
Can save translated image output for the pic-translate scene and return the saved path.
limitations: Requires Python 3, network access, and a configured SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY.
Uploads image content to a third-party Quark Scan service.
Processes one image per call and enforces a 5 MB image size limit.
Recognition quality depends on image clarity and upstream OCR service behavior.

use_cases.title: Digitize invoices and tickets
use_cases.description: Extract buyer, seller, amount, travel, and line item details from supported invoice and ticket images.

use_cases.title: Convert document photos to text
use_cases.description: Turn screenshots, scans, handwritten notes, and tables into reusable text or structured fields.

use_cases.title: Process identity and compliance documents
use_cases.description: Read supported IDs, business licenses, certificates, medical reports, and inspection reports from images.

prompt_templates.title: Extract basic text
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a screenshot or simple document image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the text from this image and return the OCR result without rewriting it: [image path or URL].

prompt_templates.title: Read a table image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for rows and columns from a photographed table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recognize the table in this image and preserve the row and column structure: [image path or URL].

prompt_templates.title: Parse an invoice
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the key fields from this invoice image, including parties, dates, amounts, and line items: [image path or URL].

prompt_templates.title: Translate image text
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs translated image output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate the text in this image while preserving the original layout, then return the translated image path and recognized content: [image path or URL].

output_examples.input: Recognize a photo of a business license.
output_examples.output: The result includes business name, credit code, representative, address, and other available license fields.

output_examples.input: Extract a photographed table from a report.
output_examples.output: The result provides table text with row and column structure when the upstream OCR service can detect it.
The result includes recognized text and a local path to the translated image when translation output is returned.

best_practices: Use clear images with readable text and minimal glare.
Choose the most specific scene for IDs, invoices, tables, formulas, or translation.
Review privacy requirements before sending sensitive images to the third-party OCR service.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for image generation or image editing tasks.
Do not send confidential images unless third-party processing is approved.
Do not batch many files in one prompt because the CLI handles one image per call.

faq.question: Does this skill work without an API key?
faq.answer: No. It requires SCAN_WEBSERVICE_KEY in the environment or in the configured key file.

faq.question: Where are images sent?
faq.answer: Images are sent to the Quark Scan business OCR endpoint used by the Python client.

faq.question: Can it process local files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read a user-specified local image file, encode it, and send it for OCR.

faq.question: Can it process multiple images at once?
faq.answer: No. The documented CLI expects one URL, path, or base64 input per execution.

faq.question: Does it save files locally?
faq.answer: Normal OCR scenes print results only. The pic-translate scene can save a translated image under the temp directory.

faq.question: Which agents are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
